appraisal_events.evidence: "Oh ! ce n'est pas grave, ce n'est que la septième fois" ... "Il s'est consolé en voulant faire un nouvel enfant à sa femme."
appraisal_events.explanation: The duc dismisses the general's repeated electoral defeat with flip mockery and caps it with a demeaning joke about his private consolation, treating a serial failure as a source of amusement.

appraisal_events.evidence: le duc qui, ayant dû lui-même renoncer à la politique, aimait assez les insuccès électoraux des autres
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator explicitly ties the duc's enjoyment of others' electoral failures to his own abandoned political career, exposing petty schadenfreude behind his mockery.

status_effects.explanation: The general is locally diminished as an object of dismissive amusement over his repeated electoral losses and personal life.
The narrator's aside quietly lowers the duc by revealing his mockery as compensatory schadenfreude rooted in his own failed political ambitions.

ambiguities: The general mocked here (referred to only as 'le général'/'ce pauvre général') is identifiable from prior context as général de Monserfeuil, but he has no entry on the reference sheet, so he is left as an unresolved surface-form character rather than merged with 'général de Froberville'.

The unattributed final line ('Il s'est consolé en voulant faire un nouvel enfant à sa femme.') has no speech tag; it is read here as a continuation of the duc's mockery, but it could alternatively belong to the princesse de Parme or be narratorial.
